reviews.comment: I took GEOG352 a few years ago. His lectures were thorough and I learned a lot. He actually wants his students to succeed. Lyle has also been very insightful and helpful to me in preparing for grad school. There is a lot of opportunity to learn and succeed with him, but you have to put the effort in and you will be challenged. Great professor.

Lots of math related to coordinate systems and geodesy, but I wish we got to mess more with software. Labs were very straightforward and easy. He tries to model his exams after the FE and FS exam so they're pretty tough, but you get to retry the exam for extra credit. Lyle is overall a great guy and it should be an easy A if you just do the work.

As long as you do the work you will get an A in this class, but you probably wont learn very much. He's an interesting and nice guy but not a very good lecturer. His exams cover material that isn't covered in class but you get to retake them so it's no sweat. The lab portion of this class is pretty easy as well. Take him but don't expect to learn
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lyle is a very knowledgeable and funny guy, but I did not feel that I learned very much from his class. The labs involve just following a checklist, and some of the homework involved finding information from government websites without any further guidance. Then the tests were riddled with grammar or technical mistakes and unreasonable questions.
Lyle is dyslexic and has a bit of autism. The class is easy to an A, just do the work!
This dude is autistic, but the class is easy.

Lyle is alright. I felt like grading was too harsh at times but you have the opportunity to redo the assignment and get it regraded anyways. The class consists of tutorial step by step instructions to follow and replicate. I felt like I learned alot of civil3d but I wish he taught more of the conceptual side of what we were actually doing.
Easy A if you go to class, still pretty easy if you don't go to class, but way easier if you go. A ton of extra credit and he knows the material very well. Great prof would take again if I could.

Lyle is the goat because his grading policy makes it easy to get an A regardless of what you get on the tests. However, I have to say he is very unorganized at times, and honestly, his teaching abilities are lacking. He makes up for it because he has a hilarious personality, and the class is an easy A if you do a large amount of assignments.

The grading system is a bit confusing. The labs are straightforward, but it might depend on the TA. He's kind of all over the place during lectures, so if you're just studying based on those, you may not do to well. Exams and quizzes were online and open note and open internet. There's a daily assignment so you have to go to class to get credit.

Very easy class, much better for CVEN 303 than 250. The tests are designed to be really hard but he offers a ton of extra credit. Labs can be frustrating sometimes due to unclear instructions but overall, great professor, especially for this class. He knows a lot about the material and really wants to help you.

Grading is unique but easy, he takes your number of points earned and divides it by 2400 points, but he offers 3000 total points so its super easy to get an A. Extremely knowledgeable about material. He is a little disorganized which can lead to confusing lectures but it didn't inhibit me that much. Overall great prof

One of the best profs I've ever had. Super friendly guy and really wants his students to succeed. His lectures are entertaining and he gives a lot of extra credit. It's hard to fail his course than it is to get an A. Definitely worth taking.

Lyle is a good lecturer and great mentor! He has a great way of breaking down concepts to their very core, making them easier to understand. Tons of opportunity for good credit, and while the class structure was occasionally difficult to understand, everything was simple enough to do and figure out. Try, and you will succeed in CVEN 250!

Professor Lyle is an extremely qualified civil engineer who's deeply passionate about what he does. He offers a lot of extra credit and definitely cares about his students. I had him for CVEN 303, so the lab's themselves rely heavily in the hands of your TAs. Good professor would take again.

Dr. Lyle has been my favorite professor at A&M. He is personable and is fun during lecture. His classes are typically lab heavy. For CVEN 303 a huge chunk of our grades was lab work. As long as you show up to the labs and put in decent effort into getting them done you should be alright. Definitely take Lyle for 250 and 303. 5/5.

Dr. Lyle has become one of my favorite profs! He is very passionate about GNSS and is easily the smartest person I know. He makes this class very interesting. Labs and in-class work are fine, however the exams are difficult but you can retake them. He also assigns a semester project that I suggest working on sooner rather than later.
He's a really fun prof who makes the class really relevant to the major and his career field. He lets you retake all assignments to a 100 and makes class really simple and work at your own pace.
Dr. Lyle is very knowlagesbale of everthing. He so nice and smart and kind and lovnig ai wlvoe him

This class is quite difficult by Lyle truly wants everyone to succeed. Was always available outside of class to help. Obviously very smart and knowledgeable. And he's goofy. Probably the best professor ive had in college so far.

Dr. Lyle was a solid choice for CVEN 303. Hes a very friendly and passionate professor who cares a great deal about his students and the work he does. His tests are difficult but he gives plenty of extra credit to make up for that. The homework isnt too bad either. If you have the opportunity to take his class definitely do it!

The labs are easy and the exams were a little tough, but he lets you retake them for extra credit rather than a replacement grade so it really boosts your grade. There's a semester long research project but it's easy if you pick a topic you like (it's open ended). Overall a solid choice, just wish the material was easier to understand.

Solid professor. Took him for civil engineering measurement and he is passionate about surveying. His class worked under a point system and he provided a good amount of extra credit opportunities that helped our grades. His lectures were also very straightforward and he would end the zoom call early once he got through the material.

He's a great guy who cares about more than academia. Granted extensions when I got sick, cares about students beyond their grades. I took him during COVID and he gave an honest discussion about mental health. It was refreshing to hear that instead of "I know these are troubling times" crap. Civil3D was hard at first for me, but use Office Hours!

Dr. Lyle is a very knowledgeable industry professional, but he assigns too much homework, his lectures aren't often helpful, and his written instructions/test questions are usually somewhere between 'hard to read' and 'illegible.'
Take Lyle, you work for your A, but he wants you to have it, gives plenty of extra credit and the labs are fun too.

Dr. Lyle is a great prof, and GEOG 352 is a very rewarding class. He has done so much in the professional world and integrates valuable skills into the class. It's a lot of work for a 3-hour course but he gives tons of chances for extra credit for you to earn the grade you want. There's a ton of stuff to keep track of in the class so stay on it!
will make you question your sanity by constantly changing formats and due dates for test and quizzes

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. He is a very knowledgeable person in his field but a terrible teacher. He used this weird 'adaptive learning' method for our class which was basically a nightmare. We took the final in the 1st week and then re-took it later. I didn't learn a lot in this class as I was lost in confusion doing out-of-context homework and projects.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Lyle was the most accessible professor I have ever had through an online course. He had no problem answering your questions via email, text, or phone call. He is very knowledgeable and willing to work with you if your job causes you to fall behind. Highly recommend him if you want to learn from someone passionate about their field.
